name: Login token saved in localStorage
why: Any script on the page (or an injected one) can read localStorage and steal the user's login.
fix: Store session tokens in HttpOnly cookies set by the server.

name: document.write used
why: Writing raw text into the page can run attacker scripts (XSS) and slows page loading.
fix: Build elements with the DOM API or your framework.

name: postMessage sends to every website (*)
why: Any site that opened your page can receive the message data.
fix: Pass your exact origin instead of '*'.

name: Link opens new tab without rel=noopener
why: The opened page can take control of your page (tab-nabbing).
fix: Add rel="noopener noreferrer".

name: Inline event handler in HTML
why: Inline handlers block a strict Content-Security-Policy and ease XSS.
fix: Attach events in JavaScript with addEventListener.

name: External script loaded without integrity check
why: If that CDN is hacked, its code runs on your site with full access.
fix: Add integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin, or host the file yourself.

name: Insecure http:// resource (mixed content)
why: Attackers on the network can swap this file or read the data.
fix: Use https:// for every resource.

name: Password field shown as plain text
why: Passwords are visible on screen and saved by browsers as normal text.
fix: Use type="password".

name: javascript: link
why: javascript: URLs run code and are a common XSS path.
fix: Use a normal link or a button with an event listener.

name: Sensitive value printed to console
why: Console logs are visible to every user and end up in logging tools.
fix: Remove the log or never print secrets.

name: Predictable token made with Math.random
why: Math.random is guessable, so attackers can predict tokens.
fix: Use crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.randomBytes().

name: javascript: URL in CSS
why: Old browsers can run script from CSS URLs.
fix: Remove it.

name: Stylesheet imported over http://
why: Attackers on the network can inject styles that hide or fake page content.
fix: Use https:// or host the file locally.

name: @import in CSS slows rendering
why: Each @import waits for the previous file, so the page shows later.
fix: Use <link> tags or bundle the CSS.

name: JWT decoded without verifying
why: decode does not check the signature, so anyone can forge a token.
fix: Use jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms list.

name: JWT verify without allowed algorithms
why: Without an algorithms list, a forged token may be accepted.
fix: Pass { algorithms: ['HS256'] } (or your algorithm).

name: Error stack sent to the user
why: Shows attackers your folder layout and libraries.
fix: Send a generic message, log the stack on the server.

name: Open redirect
why: Attackers craft links on your domain that send users to fake login pages.
fix: Redirect only to a fixed list of allowed paths.

name: User input used as a file path
why: Attackers can read any file on your server (../../.env).
fix: Validate against an allow-list and use path.basename.

name: Server fetches a URL chosen by the user (SSRF)
why: Attackers make your server call internal services or cloud metadata.
fix: Allow only known hosts and block private IP ranges.

name: Database filter taken straight from the request (NoSQL injection)
why: Attackers send {"$ne": null} operators to bypass logins and read data.
fix: Pick fields explicitly and cast them to strings.

name: Cookie flag turned off
why: The cookie can be read by scripts or sent over plain http.
fix: Set httpOnly: true and secure: true.

name: Passwords compared in plain text
why: This means passwords are stored unhashed, so one leak exposes every account.
fix: Hash with bcrypt or argon2 and compare with bcrypt.compare.

name: Weak session secret
why: Attackers can forge session cookies.
fix: Use a long random secret from .env.

name: pickle loads untrusted data
why: Loading pickle data from users runs attacker code.
fix: Use JSON instead.

name: yaml.load without SafeLoader
why: Can run attacker code from a YAML file.
fix: Use yaml.safe_load.

name: Shell command from os.system/popen
why: Attackers can run any command on your server.
fix: Use subprocess.run([...]) with a list and validate input.

name: subprocess with shell=True
why: Shell mode turns input into commands (command injection).
fix: Pass a list of arguments and drop shell=True.

name: SQL built with f-string / format / %
why: Attackers change your query to read or delete all data (SQL injection).
fix: Use placeholders: cur.execute('... WHERE id = %s', (uid,)).

name: Flask/Django debug mode
why: Debug mode exposes an interactive console to attackers.
fix: Turn debug off in production via environment variable.

name: Predictable token made with random module
why: The random module is guessable.
fix: Use the secrets module (secrets.token_urlsafe()).

name: Django allows every host / disables CSRF
why: Opens host-header and CSRF attacks.
fix: List your real domains and keep CSRF protection on.

name: User input used as a file path
why: Attackers can read any file on the server.
fix: Validate filenames with werkzeug.utils.secure_filename and an allow-list.

name: Template marks content as safe
why: Unescaped content allows XSS.
fix: Remove |safe or sanitize first.

name: include/require with user input
why: Attackers can run their own code on your server.
fix: Map allowed page names to fixed files.

name: unserialize on user data
why: Can run attacker code (object injection).
fix: Use json_decode.

name: SQL built from $_GET/$_POST
why: Attackers change your query to steal or delete data.
fix: Use prepared statements (PDO or mysqli).

name: Shell command with variable
why: Attackers can run any command on your server.
fix: Avoid shell calls or use escapeshellarg with fixed commands.

name: User input printed without escaping (XSS)
why: Attackers run scripts in your visitors' browsers.
fix: Wrap with htmlspecialchars($x, ENT_QUOTES).

name: display_errors turned on
why: Error pages reveal file paths and database details.
fix: Set display_errors=0 in production.

name: Removed mysql_* functions
why: Old unsafe API with no prepared statements.
fix: Switch to PDO or mysqli prepared statements.

name: File upload without checks
why: Attackers can upload a .php file and run it.
fix: Allow-list extensions and MIME types and store uploads outside the web root.

name: SQL built with fmt.Sprintf
why: SQL injection lets attackers read or delete data.
fix: Use placeholders: db.Query("... WHERE id = $1", id).

name: TLS certificate checks disabled
why: Anyone on the network can read or change the secure traffic.
fix: Remove it and trust proper certificates.

name: Shell started with sh -c
why: Command injection if any input reaches the string.
fix: Call the program directly with separate arguments.

name: Predictable token from math/rand
why: math/rand is guessable.
fix: Use crypto/rand.

name: HTTP server without timeouts
why: Slow clients can hold connections open and freeze your server (slowloris).
fix: Use http.Server{ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout, IdleTimeout}.

name: http.Get without timeout
why: A slow remote server can hang your request forever.
fix: Use an http.Client with Timeout.

name: template.HTML skips escaping
why: Unescaped content allows XSS.
fix: Let html/template escape automatically.

name: User input used as a file path
why: Attackers can read any file on the server.
fix: Clean the path and check it stays inside an allowed folder.

name: Weak hash (MD5/SHA1)
why: MD5/SHA1 can be cracked in seconds, bad for passwords.
fix: Use bcrypt, argon2 or scrypt for passwords.

name: GRANT ALL privileges
why: The app user can drop or read every database.
fix: Grant only the permissions the app needs.

name: Password column stored as plain text type
why: If it stores real passwords, one leak exposes all accounts.
fix: Store a hash (password_hash) made with bcrypt or argon2.

name: DROP TABLE/DATABASE in a script
why: A mistaken run deletes data permanently.
fix: Keep destructive statements out of app code and back up first.

name: Database user created with hardcoded password
why: The password is now in your repository.
fix: Create users from a secret manager or env variable.

name: Row Level Security disabled
why: Anyone with your public key can read every row (common Supabase leak).
fix: Enable RLS and add per-user policies.

name: Policy lets everyone in
why: using (true) allows every user to read every row.
fix: Restrict with auth.uid() = user_id.

name: UPDATE without WHERE
why: Changes every row in the table.
fix: Add a WHERE clause.

name: DELETE without WHERE
why: Deletes every row in the table.
fix: Add a WHERE clause.

name: Blocking file/command call
why: Sync calls freeze the whole server while they run.
fix: Use the async versions (fs.promises) inside request handlers.

name: Database call inside a loop (N+1 queries)
why: 100 items means 100 database calls: pages get slow as data grows.
fix: Fetch everything at once (WHERE id IN (...), include/join).

name: SELECT * pulls every column
why: Sends unneeded data (and can leak private columns) and slows queries.
fix: List only the columns you need.

name: Query with no limit
why: Returns the whole table; slow and memory-heavy once data grows.
fix: Add limit/pagination.

name: HTTP request without timeout (requests)
why: A slow remote server hangs your app forever.
fix: Pass timeout=10.

name: Deep copy with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())
why: Slow on large objects and drops dates/functions.
fix: Use structuredClone().

name: Whole library imported (big bundle)
why: Adds hundreds of KB to the frontend and slows first load.
fix: Import single functions (lodash/debounce) or use date-fns/dayjs.

name: Image without loading=lazy
why: All images download at once, so the page is slower.
fix: Add loading="lazy" and width/height.

name: Very fast setInterval
why: Timers under 200ms burn CPU and battery.
fix: Use a longer interval or requestAnimationFrame.

name: LIKE with leading wildcard
why: Cannot use an index, so the table is scanned every time.
fix: Use full-text search or a trigram index.

name: time.sleep in Python code
why: In a web request this blocks the worker.
fix: Use background tasks or async sleep.

name: Reminder to add security later
why: Skipped security work is easy to forget before launch.
fix: Do the task now.

name: Authentication bypass switch
why: A bypass flag left on in production gives everyone access.
fix: Remove it, or make sure it is off outside local dev.

name: Default admin credentials
why: Default logins are the first thing attackers try.
fix: Create a strong unique password from an env variable.

name: Whole request body saved to the database
why: A user can add extra fields (role: admin, price: 0) because nothing says they can't.
fix: Whitelist the exact fields each endpoint may set.

name: Record fetched by an ID from the request
why: If it does not also check who owns the record, changing the ID shows someone else's data (IDOR).
fix: Also filter by the logged-in user's ID and return not-found if it is not theirs.

name: Whole request body passed to a model
why: A user can set fields like role or price by adding them to the request.
fix: Pass only an explicit list of allowed fields.

name: File upload with no size limit
why: One huge upload can freeze the app for everyone.
fix: Set limits: { fileSize: ... } and check the real file type.

name: Upload saved under the user's file name
why: Attackers choose the name and path of the file on your server.
fix: Save under a random name outside the app folder, after checking the real type.
